statement: Angle $\theta$ satisfies $\pi < \theta < \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ and $\sin\theta = -\dfrac{5}{13}$. What is the value of $\tan(2\theta)$? (Note: $\tan(2\theta) = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$.)

choices.misconception: I used a positive cosine and got $\tan\theta = -\frac{5}{12}$, but in the third quadrant sine and cosine are both negative, so $\tan\theta = \frac{5}{12}$.
I doubled $\tan\theta = \frac{5}{12}$ to get $\frac{5}{6}$, as if $\tan(2\theta)$ were just $2\tan\theta$.
I found $\sin(2\theta) = \frac{120}{169}$ and $\cos(2\theta) = \frac{119}{169}$ correctly, but then I divided cosine by sine instead of sine by cosine.

hints: First find $\cos\theta$. Which sign must it have when $\theta$ is between $\pi$ and $\frac{3\pi}{2}$?
Use $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ with a negative cosine, find $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$, then use the given identity.

solutions.reliable: From $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$, $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \frac{25}{169} = \frac{144}{169}$. In the third quadrant cosine is negative, so $\cos\theta = -\frac{12}{13}$ and $\tan\theta = \frac{-5/13}{-12/13} = \frac{5}{12}$. Then $\tan(2\theta) = \dfrac{2 \cdot \frac{5}{12}}{1 - \frac{25}{144}} = \dfrac{\frac{10}{12}}{\frac{119}{144}} = \frac{10}{12} \cdot \frac{144}{119} = \frac{120}{119}$.
solutions.elegant: Check with double angles: $\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2\left(-\frac{5}{13}\right)\left(-\frac{12}{13}\right) = \frac{120}{169}$ and $\cos(2\theta) = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta = 1 - \frac{50}{169} = \frac{119}{169}$, so $\tan(2\theta) = \frac{120}{119}$.
